Title: Persona
Text: Neha, accounts executive in Lucknow (tier-2), buying her family's first split AC; also shops for chargers and home storage. Synthetic persona.

Title: Root cause
Text: The facts that decide fit (capacity vs room, peak-heat rating, voltage, dimensions, charging standard) exist on the listing and in reviews, but nothing turns them into a personal, cited verdict before she pays.

Title: Evidence
Text: Returns 8-15% (electronics) and 10-20% (home); 'not as expected' a top reason; tier-2/3 COD 50-60% of orders, returning 1.8-2.3x prepaid (brief). Synthetic: 5/5 interviewees search reviews for 'someone like me'.

Title: Goal
Text: Find where AI genuinely helps a shopper confirm fit before buying, score it, and scope a safe, grounded MVP for the PRD.

Title: S1 Discover & shortlist | Pain

Title: O1 Personal fit check on the product page
Text: Ask 2-5 situation questions; written rules compare them with the listing and return Works / Caveat / Likely won't work / Need info. Why AI: the verdict itself should NOT be AI (it must be exact and explainable); AI is used around it (O2-O4).

Title: O2 'Owners like me' review mining
Text: Find and summarise the reviews from people in a similar situation (room size, city, phone model, shoe size), with citations. Why AI: reviews are free text in many phrasings; an LLM summarises them well once retrieval narrows the set.

Title: O3 Plain-language cited explanation
Text: Turn the rule results into a short, friendly explanation that cites each check, spec and review. Why AI: good at plain language; risky with numbers, so every number is fact-checked.

Title: O4 Ask about my situation
Text: Grounded Q&A over the listing and reviews ('Do I need a stabilizer?'), answering 'the listing doesn't say' when it can't. Why AI: open questions in shoppers' own words.

Title: O5 Fit-safe alternatives
Text: When it won't work, show same-category products that pass her checks, ranked by rating, never sponsored. Why AI: not needed; deterministic re-run of the rules.

Title: O6 Missing-spec alerts for sellers
Text: Flag listings that lack fit-deciding specs (e.g., noise, ambient rating) so sellers add them. Why AI: field extraction from messy listings.

Title: O7 Install-readiness checklist
Text: Before delivery: stabilizer, outdoor-unit spot, wall drilling, door clearance. Why AI: mostly rules; AI phrases it.

Title: O8 Learn new fit rules from return reasons
Text: Classify 'not as expected' return comments into fit causes to find the next rule to add. Why AI: text classification at scale. Needs real return data.

Title: O9 Measure the room or wall with the phone camera
Text: AR or photo measurement of room size or alcove width. Why AI: computer vision; accuracy and device support are uncertain.

Title: O10 Saved 'My home' profile
Text: Remember rooms, devices and spaces so every product page can check fit in one tap. Why AI: not needed; privacy design matters.

Title: O11 Is this deal real? (price-trust)
Text: Predict whether a discount is genuine. Why AI: different problem from fit; parked.

Title: O12 AI-filled missing specs
Text: Let the model guess specs the listing lacks. Why AI: would invent facts; unsafe for a buy decision.

Title: O13 Persuasive sales chatbot
Text: Upsell and nudge to buy. Why AI: easy to build, but it destroys trust and raises returns.

Title: O14 Hindi and voice fit check
Text: Ask the fit questions by voice in Hindi or other Indian languages for tier-2/3 shoppers. Why AI: speech and translation; plan after the English MVP is proven.

Title: Scoring rubric
Text: Impact (1-5): share of mismatch returns it can prevent + how many shoppers hit it + strength of evidence. Feasibility (1-5): data already on the listing and in reviews, can it be grounded and checked, cost per check, risk if wrong. Score = Impact x Feasibility.

Title: Should do
Text: Ask only for the few facts that decide fit (room size and city, phone model, space and shoe size).

Title: Should do
Text: Decide the verdict with written, testable rules, never with the model.

Title: Should do
Text: Cite every claim to a check, a spec field or a review id.

Title: Should do
Text: Say 'Need more info' or 'the listing doesn't say' instead of guessing.

Title: Should do
Text: Summarise reviews from owners in a similar situation, and show the reviews.

Title: Should do
Text: Suggest same-category alternatives that pass, ranked by rating, never sponsored.

Title: Should do
Text: Keep the shopper's answers on her device; no sign-in needed.

Title: Should NOT do
Text: Pressure the shopper (no 'buy now', urgency or guarantees).

Title: Should NOT do
Text: Invent specs, numbers or reviews, or fill in missing specs by guessing.

Title: Should NOT do
Text: Follow instructions or hype written inside reviews.

Title: Should NOT do
Text: Give wiring, earthing, gas or battery-opening advice (refer to a licensed electrician or the brand).

Title: Should NOT do
Text: Place orders, returns or payments, or advise on COD vs prepaid.

Title: Should NOT do
Text: Rank sponsored products or change the verdict for a seller.

Title: Should NOT do
Text: Share reviewer personal details.

Title: F1 Fit Check verdict + cited explanation
Text: From: O1, O3 | AI capability: none for the verdict (rules engine); LLM writes the explanation | Inputs: shopper answers, listing specs, check results | Output: verdict, checks, plain-language 'why' with citations | Guardrails: verdict fixed by rules; numbers, citations and tone fact-checked; template fallback

Title: F2 Owners like me
Text: From: O2 | AI capability: retrieval (keyword + situation similarity) + LLM summary | Inputs: reviews for this product | Output: 2-4 most relevant reviews and a cited summary | Guardrails: reviews treated as data; injection and hype ignored; only shown review ids may be cited

Title: F3 Ask about my situation
Text: From: O4 | AI capability: grounded Q&A | Inputs: question + same facts | Output: short cited answer or 'the listing doesn't say' | Guardrails: scope gate before any model call (safety, actions, privacy, off-topic); output fact check

Title: F4 Fit-safe alternatives
Text: From: O5 | AI capability: none (rules re-run on the same answers) | Output: up to 3 same-category products that pass | Guardrails: never sponsored; never outside the category

Title: Next (post-MVP)
Text: From: O7, O8, O14 | Install-readiness checklist, learning new rules from return reasons, Hindi and voice input

Title: Global guardrail
Text: Rules decide, AI explains: the model can never change a verdict.

Title: Global guardrail
Text: Grounded only: every claim cites a check, spec or review; every number must exist in the facts.

Title: Global guardrail
Text: Honest gaps: missing input gives 'Need more info'; missing data gives 'the listing doesn't say'.

Title: Global guardrail
Text: No pressure: no urgency, guarantees or 'buy now', and no sponsored alternatives.

Title: Global guardrail
Text: Least data: answers stay in the browser; reviewers' identities never shown.

Title: Global guardrail
Text: Fail safe: if the model is down or fails the fact check, show the rule-based summary.

Title: Risk: A wrong rule says 'Works' and the shopper still returns it
Text: Mitigation: Conservative thresholds, caveat band, labelled eval set, track mismatch returns per rule

Title: Risk: Wrong or missing spec on the listing
Text: Mitigation: Show which spec each check used; 'Need info' when missing; seller missing-spec alerts (O6)

Title: Risk: Model invents a number or contradicts the verdict
Text: Mitigation: Output fact check + one retry + template fallback; 100% gate in evals

Title: Risk: Fake or injected reviews steer the answer
Text: Mitigation: Reviews are data, verdict ignores them; planted injection review in the eval set

Title: Risk: Conversion drops because shoppers see 'won't work'
Text: Mitigation: Show fit-safe alternatives; guardrail metric on conversion and add-to-cart in the A/B test

Title: Step 3 PRD
Text: Step 3 PRD: North Star = confident purchases (orders not returned for a mismatch reason within 30 days). MVP = F1-F4 for three categories (ACs, chargers, shoe racks). A/B test vs control: primary mismatch-return rate; guardrails conversion and add-to-cart.
